text:
andrew: pushed PR #6850 to change the alloc scheduler's microbatch window. small refactor + one config flip. canarying now, need quick perf eyes before merge :eyes:
deploy-bot: canary deployed pr-6850 -> staging (canary-id: c-319) at 2026-03-15T10:12:08Z
marta: ran the long-seq perf job against the canary (seq=4096). quick summary: p50 ~120ms (no change), p95 120ms -> 140ms (+16%), p99 220ms -> 260ms (+18%). throughput steady. attaching raw bench below. :thinking_face:
jia: posting the bench command + output:
```bash
# runner: bench-longseq --model rdx-small --seq 4096 --concurrency 16 --runs 300
baseline (main): p50=118ms p95=121ms p99=221ms qps=42.3
canary (c-319): p50=119ms p95=140ms p99=260ms qps=41.9
```
sam: looks like a tail regression rather than bulk throughput. did you change the KV cache path or scheduling window?
andrew: only change was scheduler: batch_window_ms default 5 -> 8 and a small allocator path dedupe. i thought bigger window would help throughput for short bursts, not hurt longseq.
ben: can you run the same bench with batch_window=6 and 7 to see trend? might be a nonlinear tail effect.
marta: i ran extra runs (6 and 7):
```
batch_window=5 -> p95=121ms p99=221ms
batch_window=6 -> p95=130ms p99=240ms
batch_window=7 -> p95=136ms p99=252ms
batch_window=8 -> p95=140ms p99=260ms
```
ben: aha. looks monotonic. slight increase after 5. suggests batching adds a bit to tail for long sequences under concurrency.
jia: can we quantify user impact? most customers use seq<=2048. i re-ran seq=2048 on canary: p95 unchanged (68ms -> 69ms) p99 +5%. so small effect for shorter seqs.
andrew: thanks — given this, i can either revert the default to 5 or make it adaptive per-seq-length. i can push change in the PR if folks are ok.
sam: i'd prefer revert default for stability and follow up with adaptive in a follow-up PR. lower risk.
marta: agree. revert default -> then rerun canary. if tail goes back to baseline we can merge.
andrew: ok i'll push a small commit to restore default 5 and add a TODO comment to track adaptive batching. pinging for reviews: @ben @jia @marta please review last commit when it's up. need 2 LGTMs to merge.
ben: will review after lunch, likely :+1:.
jia: will check perf and code, leaving notes if anything.
marta: once revert commit is deployed to canary, i'll run a quick smoke bench and report.
deploy-bot: canary deployed pr-6850 (revert-default) -> staging (canary-id: c-320) at 2026-03-15T12:03:10Z
marta: smoke results for c-320 (seq=4096): p95=122ms p99=224ms qps=42.2 -> basically back to baseline. :white_check_mark:
andrew: thanks all. @ben @jia need final LGTMs to merge. i'll hold if anyone wants more tests.
ben: LGTM
jia: LGTM
andrew: merging in ~10m, will watch canary metrics and roll out. will open follow-up for adaptive batching. :rocket:
marta: monitoring dashboards set, will alert if tail drifts.
sam: thanks everyone, good catch.
andrew: :thumbsup:
